findings.title: Delete and Pause menu items never render in the alert list view because they are gated on rulerRule
findings.body: The Delete item is rendered under the condition `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165), and the Pause item under `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && ...` (line 123). This PR changes the list view so that GrafanaRuleListItem -> RuleActionsButtons.V2 -> AlertRuleMenu is given only `promRule` (rulerRule is undefined; see GrafanaRuleListItem's `actions: <RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule}.../>`). With `rulerRule` undefined both guards are false, so Delete and Pause disappear from the list even when the new prom-rule abilities make `canDelete`/`canPause` true. This is a regression from the previous GrafanaGroupLoader/GrafanaRuleLoader behavior, which loaded the ruler rule and passed it down. The guard is also stale: in RuleActionsButtons.V2 `handleDelete={() => showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)}` ignores the rulerRule argument entirely, so Delete can be rendered and handled without a rulerRule. PauseMenuItem only needs the ruler rule object to perform its mutation, so if pausing must stay functional in the list it needs to fetch the ruler rule on demand rather than silently hide the item.

findings.title: Grafana branch of the rules list lost its React key
findings.body: In the `rules.map(...)` render, the `origin === 'grafana'` branch previously rendered `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ... />` but now renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} ... />` without a `key`. The surrounding `datasource` and default branches still pass `key={key}`. Rendering a mapped array without keys produces React reconciliation warnings and, more importantly, lets React reuse component instances between rows. Each row contains RuleActionsButtons.V2, which keeps local state (delete modal, silence drawer, clone redirect); during infinite-scroll appends or list mutations this can cause state to bleed across rows (for example a delete/silence dialog belonging to the wrong rule). Add `key={key}` to the GrafanaRuleListItem.

findings.title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
findings.body: `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` previously computed `const isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group);`. The refactor to take a `RulerRuleDTO | undefined` plus a `RuleGroupIdentifierV2` no longer has access to the group object, so it now hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` (line 245, with a TODO). Federated rule groups (Mimir Enterprise cross-tenant federation, identified by `source_tenants`) can only be modified through the ruler on the owning tenant and were intentionally made read-only in Grafana by feeding `isFederated` into the `immutableRule` calculation. With this change `immutableRule` is false for federated rules, so Update/Pause/Restore/Delete abilities become allowed for them and users can attempt edits that Grafana cannot correctly persist. The group's `source_tenants` needs to be threaded through to keep federated rules immutable.

findings.title: Test grants delete permission but asserts Delete is absent, locking in the deletion regression
findings.body: The `should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked` test grants `AlertingRuleDelete` (and true folder delete access in `setFolderAccessControl`) and then asserts the menu contains exactly 4 items (`expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)`) - silence, copy link, duplicate, export - i.e. it explicitly expects the Delete item to be missing. This encodes the bug where Delete/Pause are hidden because the list view no longer supplies a rulerRule (see AlertRuleMenu). Because of this assertion, fixing Delete in the list will make the test fail, so it should instead assert that the Delete menu item is present when the user has the delete permission.
